intended_object: The block substitution (block composition) of multivariate polynomials: for p ∈ R[x_i : i ∈ ι] and q ∈ R[y_k : k ∈ κ], it is the polynomial p(q(x_{i,·}))_{i∈ι} ∈ R[x_{(i,k)}]. Each variable x_i of p is replaced by a copy of q in its own block of fresh variables x_{(i,k)}. This reading comes from the docstring, the module documentation and the lemma `eval_blockSubst`.
explanation:
The body is `bind₁ (fun i => rename (Prod.mk i) q) p`. This is the algebra homomorphism that sends each variable X_i to `rename (Prod.mk i) q`, the copy of q whose variables are relabelled to (i, k), applied to p. So it is exactly p(q(X_{(i,·)}))_i. The lemma `eval_blockSubst` confirms the intended meaning: evaluating at x gives p evaluated at the values q(x(i,·)).

The setting is already fully general. R only needs to be a commutative semiring, which is what `bind₁` and `rename` require, and ι and κ are arbitrary types. Degenerate cases also behave correctly:
- If p is constant, the result is that constant.
- If ι is empty, the result is a constant polynomial over the empty set of variables.

Mathlib has `bind₁` and `rename`, but no named construction for this particular block composition, so there is no more general Mathlib counterpart.
